facts.text: Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-1) was deployed at Hadley Rille during Apollo 15 in 1971.

The first car on the Moon. A battery-powered, wire-mesh-wheeled buggy that let Scott and Irwin drive up to 12 km from the LM. Top speed: 13 km/h. Its TV camera, aimed by Houston, filmed the ascent stage liftoff.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Extended the exploration radius from roughly 1 km on foot to over 5 km, enabling collection of diverse geological samples from the rille edge, Apennine mountain front, and multiple craters.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Hadley Rille.
Parked at its final position with the TV camera aimed to film the ascent stage liftoff; remains one of only three cars on the Moon.
